name: Alaska
math: $200.00 a day x 5 working days (at most 90)
rule: the regular wage from the time of demand to the time of payment, or for 90 working days, whichever is less

name: Arizona
math: 3 x $1,000.00 recoverable in all, so $2,000.00 on top of the wages
rule: in a civil action, treble the unpaid wages

name: California
rule: if the employer willfully fails to pay, the wages continue as a penalty at the same daily rate until paid, for up to 30 days

name: Connecticut
math: 2 x $1,000.00 recoverable in all, so $1,000.00 on top of the wages
rule: in a civil action, twice the full amount of the wages

name: Delaware
math: 10% x $1,000.00 x 7 days, Sundays and holidays not counted = $700.00; capped at the unpaid wages ($1,000.00)
rule: liquidated damages of the lower of 10% of the unpaid wages for each day (except Sundays and legal holidays) the failure continues, or an amount equal to the unpaid wages

name: District of Columbia
math: 10% x $1,000.00 x 5 days, working days only = $500.00; capped at 3 x the unpaid wages ($3,000.00)
rule: liquidated damages of 10% of the unpaid wages for each working day the failure continues, or treble the unpaid wages, whichever is smaller

name: Idaho
rule: administrative penalties of up to $750 ($500 if paid before the department files a state lien)

name: Kansas
math: 1% x $1,000.00 x 1 day (after the first 8), Sundays and holidays not counted = $10.00; capped at the unpaid wages ($1,000.00)
rule: if willful, 1% of the unpaid wages for each day (except Sundays and legal holidays) after the eighth day, or 100% of the unpaid wages, whichever is less

name: Maine
math: 2 x $1,000.00 on top of the wages
rule: in a court action, the unpaid wages plus twice the unpaid wages as liquidated damages, interest, costs and fees; also a fine of $100 to $500 per violation

name: Minnesota
rule: average daily earnings for each day in default, up to 15 days

name: North Dakota
rule: the agreed wage for each day in default, ending 30 days after the default

name: Oregon
math: 8 x $25.00 an hour x 10 days (at most 30)
rule: penalty wages of eight times the regular hourly rate for each day unpaid, up to 30 days; plus a possible $1,000 civil penalty for willful failure

name: Pennsylvania
math: 10 days late: liquidated damages start once wages are unpaid 30 days beyond the regular payday
rule: wages unpaid 30 days after the regular payday (with no good-faith dispute): liquidated damages of 25% of the wages due or $500, whichever is greater

name: South Carolina
math: 3 x $1,000.00 recoverable in all, so $2,000.00 on top of the wages
rule: in a civil action, three times the unpaid wages, plus costs and attorney's fees

name: West Virginia
math: 2 x $1,000.00 on top of the wages
rule: the unpaid amount plus two times that amount as liquidated damages
